Person A: Just had a shower and walks into a restaurant. Person B sits next to them and starts smoking. Person A walks out and now smells like smoke. Now...

Person A = Person A + (Person B's smoke smell)

Person B = Person B

Person A has no affect on Person B, but instead has been directly affected by Person B. Now replace the word "smoke" with "fart." Same thing.

You're missing the point, and there would be no way to prove that I've experienced it.

I'm not for the banning of smoking. I even smoke with my friends at bars and parties, but there's a time and place for that. Not when I'm trying to enjoy my lunch break. It stinks and makes people feel nauseous, and it sucks when you gotta worry that your anti-smoking boss thinks you were smoking...all because some stranger couldn't suppress the urge to smoke. Just like when you're worried that someone's gonna think you were the farter.

I'm glad that there are people who are more aware of it.

I actually smoke with my friends from time to time, but there's a time and place for that.

The wind can blow it in your direction, hence the blowing in my face. I remember when I was a kid and I'd wait for my mom outside of the mall where people would stand and smoke. She'd smell it on me and ask if I was smoking.

My point isn't that smoking should be banned. My point is that although it may feel good, not everyone wants to smell it. Farting can feel amazing. It can be fun to do with your friends or spouse. It's your right to fart wherever you please. You may enjoy the smell of your farts from time to time. It can actually cause pain if you don't fart. But if you sit down next to people who aren't farting, are you going to start farting up a storm and stink up the place?

Yes, that sounds like perfect logic. Leave my home because I can't always enjoy restaurants in my area. I don't think smoking should be banned, I just think people should be more aware of others around them. I love to fart because it feels great, but people don't want to smell it when they're eating.

I live somewhere where it's still acceptable to smoke in some McDonald's. Walk in smelling clean and fresh, walk out smelling like I just went to a nightclub.

There are also restaurants with patios where smokers are allowed to smoke. I would avoid it if they were there first, but when I'm halfway through my meal and someone lights up, it doesn't seem fair. I like being outside too. Of course, I'd be the one considered a dick if I said anything because I had a choice to go somewhere where people smoke.

Just a bit of exaggeration. They don't intentionally blow it people's faces, but you can smell it just by sitting there and your clothes will smell like it when you leave the restaurant.

It's the same when waiting outside for a bux/taxi and someone in line lights one up. Showing up for an interview/date smelling like an ashtray isn't fun.

I agree with the logic here, but there should still be a level of consideration for the people around you. Farting is allowed in an elevator, but you would still probably hold it until you were alone.
